claims.text: Enhanced local chromium segregation at grain boundaries promotes formation of a chromium-rich passive film in duplex stainless steels.
The passive film formed as a result of grain-boundary chromium segregation is Cr2O3-rich.
The chromium-rich passive film is stable under corrosive exposure.
The chromium-rich passive film can self-heal after minor damage.
A chromium-rich passive film suppresses localized corrosion such as pitting.
The initial duplex stainless steels have a homogeneous chromium distribution at well-characterized grain boundaries.
Varying overall chromium content can be used to promote controlled chromium segregation at grain boundaries.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can promote controlled chromium segregation specifically at grain boundaries.
Acidified chloride solutions at pH 2–3 and approximately 80°C simulate aggressive chemical-processing and nuclear-power operating environments.
Increasing chromium availability at grain boundaries accelerates formation of a robust passive film.
Samples with enhanced grain-boundary chromium segregation will have lower overall corrosion rates than baseline samples.
Samples with enhanced grain-boundary chromium segregation will exhibit fewer pitting events than baseline samples.
Samples with enhanced grain-boundary chromium segregation will develop a more spatially uniform passive film than baseline samples.
Standard processing produces a uniform chromium distribution but a lower level of chromium enrichment at grain boundaries.
The proposed effect is expected to hold in acidified chloride solution at approximately 80°C but may not transfer to other environments or steel systems.
A causal chromium-segregation mechanism predicts corresponding chromium enrichment of the passive film relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes a homogeneous chromium distribution, whereas the baseline is also called uniform but is said to have a lower level of chromium enrichment at grain boundaries. Grain-boundary enrichment is inconsistent with a strictly homogeneous distribution unless 'homogeneous' is intended only as an approximation.
